facts.claim: Older adults did not show an increase in source misattributions following successful associative inference, unlike younger adults.
facts.quote: we found that older adults, in contrast to younger adults, did not show an increase in source misattributions following successful associative inference.

facts.claim: There was no overall effect of sleep on either accurate or false memories in a meta-analysis of the Deese/Roediger-McDermott paradigm.
facts.quote: the meta-analysis revealed that, whereas there was no overall effect of sleep on either accurate or false memories, the effect of sleep on overall memories was moderated by two constraints.

facts.claim: A retrieval mechanism that helps people make successful inferences also contributes to the misattribution of reward-context in memory.
facts.quote: These results suggest that a recombination-related retrieval mechanism that supports successful inference also contributes to the misattribution of reward-context in memory

facts.claim: Participants were more susceptible to false memories for contextual details after successful than unsuccessful inferential retrieval, but only when contextual details were probed after the associative inference test.
facts.quote: participants were more susceptible to false memories for contextual details after successful than unsuccessful inferential retrieval, but only when contextual details were probed after the associative inference test.

facts.claim: A group's proneness to false memories was associated with reduced representational match between the tested item and all studied items in the visual cortex.
facts.quote: the AV group’s proneness to false memories was associated with ( i ) reduced representational match between the tested item and all studied items in the visual cortex

facts.claim: False memories in immediate recognition tests were accompanied by the reduction of verbatim memory retrieval resulting from the impairment of rehearsal.
facts.quote: the occurrence of false memories in immediate recognition test was accompanied by the reduction of verbatim memory retrieval resulting from the impairment of rehearsal.

research.angle: Memory retrieval involves a recombination mechanism that allows for successful inferences but also causes source misattributions and false memories, particularly in younger adults.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that the same cognitive processes used to link different memories to make new connections also contribute to the creation of false memories and distorted contexts.
research.caveat: The effects of sleep on memory consolidation are highly dependent on specific task features and the number of items in a list.
